description:
Leaseholder of ground floor flat within Repton Park development (Grade II listed, Clayhall Conservation area) applying for listed building consent to replace a warped timber external patio door (2 leaf, external opening, each leaf 2010x490mm approx, upper half double glazed window, lower half recessed wooden panel). The warping no longer allows the two leaves of the door to meet in the midline at the top leading to security risk and excessive draughts. Two opinions have been obtained whether the warping could be rectified by refurbishing the door- replacement was stated as the only effective option. A quotation has been obtained from Banham Security for a like-for-like replacement of the doors and frame requiring them to be visually identical in design, materials and colour. Red grandis timber has been suggested and the replacement doors will be colour matched by taking a sample of the existing door and having their in-house french polisher match the appearance. (The surveyor's specification for the 2022 external redecoration of the flats on the development was for 2-3 coats of Dulux Ultimate Woodstain in walnut, Banham are aware of this but will directly colour match from the existing door).
I contacted Redbridge Planning as I wasn't sure which types of consent would be needed and Chris Anderson (Principal Technical Officer, Place Communities and Enterprise Directorate) kindly replied with the advice that listed building consent is needed but as the patio door is to the rear planning permission would probably not be required.
